patch.summary: Update an attribute-based access control category in the specified database.

Example 1.description: This example demonstrates how to update only the 'Name' property of an access control category.

Example 2.description: This example demonstrates how to specify which discrete attribute an access control category should use for a table. This request maps the table 'Tensile Test Data' (GUID = '0dd5348e-72f3-4bcb-bb38-621e5953a333') to the discrete attribute 'Test status' for this category. The existing table mapping for table 'MaterialUniverse' (GUID = '0000dd92-0011-4fff-8fff-0000ffff0000') will be unchanged. Any other existing table mappings will be deleted. To use this request, the access control category must have the discrete type 'Project Status' (GUID = '683db97e-b985-42a2-9dd8-4b77f48b1855').

Example 3.summary: Replace table mappings and table values
Example 3.description: This example demonstrates how to update table mappings, including table values. This request maps the table 'Tensile Test Data' to the discrete attribute 'Test status' for this category, and sets the table discrete value to 'Requested'. Any other existing table mappings will be deleted. To use this request, the access control category must have the discrete type 'Project Status' (GUID = '683db97e-b985-42a2-9dd8-4b77f48b1855').

Example 4.description: This request updates the table discrete value to 'Completed' in an existing table mapping for the table 'Tensile Test Data'. The attribute does not need to be specified, because the mapping already exists and so must have an attribute. Any other existing table mappings will be deleted. To use this request, the access control category must have the discrete type 'Project Status' (GUID = '683db97e-b985-42a2-9dd8-4b77f48b1855') with a table mapping for the table 'Tensile Test Data' (GUID = 0dd5348e-72f3-4bcb-bb38-621e5953a333).

Example 5.description: This example demonstrates how to delete a table mapping for the table 'Tensile Test Data', by setting the attribute to null. The mapping could also be deleted by not including it.

Example 6.description: This example demonstrates how to delete all table mappings for the access control category, by setting the tableMappings to null.

delete.summary:
Requests cancellation of a long-running operation for updating permission-based access control settings.
Cancellation will only happen when the operation is pending or in progress, and is not guaranteed - it is a best-effort attempt to stop the operation early.
The long-running operation status will be set to awaitingCancellation; then to cancelled if cancellation is successful.
If the long-running operation has already completed (succeeded or failed), an error will be returned.
If the long-running operation has already been cancelled, the status will remain as is (awaitingCancellation or cancelled).

post.summary:
Gets all target tables that match the provided link target, for each target.
There could be several matches or no matches for each link target.
For example if two databases are loaded with the same databaseGuid and the databaseVersionGuid isn't specified,
or if the databaseGuid and databaseVersionGuid are not specified and the tableGuid matches in several databases.
There could be no matches if the target database is not loaded.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: The version control mode. If not provided, defaults to write mode if the user is allowed to see that. Can also be set in the header.

parameters.name: X-Ansys-VC-Mode
parameters.description: The version control mode. If not provided, defaults to write mode if the user is allowed to see that. Can also be set in the query string.

Example 1.description: This example demonstrates how to resolve a link target that targets the MaterialUniverse table, when all GUIDs are specified.

Example 2.description: This example demonstrates how to resolve a link target that targets the MaterialUniverse table, when some GUIDs are not specified.If the DatabaseVersionGuid is not specified, the link target could resolve to more than one table if there are other database loaded that match the criteria.

GsaAggregationsRequest.description:
A request for aggregation information from a particular scope. The type of information
requested can vary: for example, for attributes, it could be a request for minimum/maximum
values, or for common text terms.
            
An aggregation request is associated with a particular scope (database, table, integration
schema, etc) based off the API invoked; however, the scope can be further narrowed down by
providing a criterion in the aggregation request. Only data from records matching that
criterion will be considered when aggregating data.
            
Note that only some types of criterion will be supported: in particular, criteria that involve
"matches" criteria against functional attributes, or link-attribute criteria against record
link groups, are not eligible to be used as an aggregation query criterion.

criterion: An optional query criterion, to be used to filter the collection of records to aggregate over.

tableSearchBehaviour: Determines the behaviour of records in tables that are marked as hidden from search. The default behaviour is that these records are excluded.

the aggregation scope that have a value for the attribute. In some cases, depending on the attribute
type, we may be able to report more information. For example, aggregating over a numeric attribute will
also provide the minimum and maximum values that attribute takes across records in the aggregation
scope.

GsaAttributeAggregationValueCriterion.description:
A criterion for requesting aggregations for a single specific attribute or meta-attribute,
including summary information about the values assumed by the attribute.
            
For a numeric attribute (integer, point, range, or date-time), the summary information will
be the minimum and maximum values assumed by the attribute on some record.
            
For a simple text attribute (discrete, short-text), the summary information will be the most
common terms in the search index for that attribute.
            
This can also be used within the inner criteria of a 'link' attribute aggregation, to request
an aggregation over a local tabular column.

- logical: exists, doesNotExist, equal, none
- picture, link, tabular: exists, doesNotExist, none
- point, range, integer, date, floatFunctional, mathsFunctional: exists, doesNotExist, atLeast, atMost, equal, between, none
- discrete: exists, doesNotExist, atLeast, atMost, equal, isOneOf, isNot, isAllOf, none
- discreteFunctional: exists, doesNotExist, atLeast, atMost, equal, isOneOf, none

createDate.description: The date and time that the update was created.

updateGuid.description: A unique identity to disambiguate this update from all other updates.

prerequisiteUpdateGuid.description: GUID for the previous update that need to have been applied before this update can be applied.

prerequisiteUpdateName.description: Name of the previous update that need to have been applied before this update can be applied.  This is used only for display purposes.

miVersion.description: Gets the version of MI that was used to create this update.

supportedObjectsVersion.description:
Gets or sets the version number indicating the kinds of object that this update supports. A client will be
able to process updates with an unrecognised SupportedObjectsVersion (although in doing so it will have to
ignore fields describing objects it does not recognise).

updateFormatVersion.description:
Gets or sets the version number of the format of the update. This will change if the meaning of any of the
fields in the update changes. A client must not process an update with an UpdateFormatVersion field that it
does not recognise, as it cannot be sure of the meaning of the fields it reads.

sourceDatabaseKey.description: Gets or sets the database key of the database from which this update was generated.

sourceVolumeGuid.description: Gets or sets the guid of the volume from which the update was generated.

name.description: Gets or sets the name of the update.

description.description: Gets or sets the description of the update.

projectName.description: Gets or sets the name of the project this update was created for.

projectGuid.description: Gets or sets the guid of the project this update was created for.

containsFallbackIdentifiers.description: Gets or sets the flag informing whether or not this update contains fallback identifiers (mostly names).

newVersionGuid.description:
Gets or sets the value Database Version GUID should be updated to.
If this field is set then we propose to retarget tabular attributes to link to new version of the database.

id.description: Gets or sets the token which identifies this job.

databaseKey.description: Gets or sets the key of the database against which this job has been / will be run.

name.description: Gets or sets the name of the update.

description.description: Gets or sets the description of the job.

timeStarted.description: Gets or sets the time that the job started.

timeCompleted.description: Gets or sets the time that the job completed.

error.description:
The error that occurred (if any) when the job was run. If the
job has not yet been run, or if the job completed successfully,
this will be null.

GsaDataUpdaterJob.description:
updateToken: Gets or sets the token which links this job to the update on which it is working.

jobType: Gets or sets the type of job.

status: Gets or sets the job status.

GsaDataUpdaterJobStatus.description:
The status of a data updater job.

Possible values:

  • Unknown: This job is in an unknown state.
  • Queued: This job is in the queue and has not been started.
  • InProgress: This job is in progress.
  • Completed: This job completed successfully.
  • Cancelled: This job was cancelled.
  • Cancelling: This job is in the process of being cancelled.
  • Failed: This job failed.
  • NotFound: This job cannot be found.

GsaDataUpdaterJobType.description:
Possible values:

  • NoAction: A job that takes no action.
  • CreateUpdate: A job that creates an update.
  • Ship: A job that ships an update.
  • DryRunUpdate: A job that performs a dry run of an update on a database.
  • ApplyUpdate: A job that applies an update to a database.

schema defines mappings or transformations from existing stored data, which may be a different
shape from the integration schema.

GsaLinkDatumCriterion.description:
link: Criterion for matching records that are linked to records that match the inner criterion. The target database and table specify the location of the linked records.
The inner criterion must be a criterion that applies to the records in the linked table. The link group followed will be the link group specified on the outer AttributeCriterion.
A target database is required unless searching local tabular data - In that case, the inner criterion must be absent, and the local criterion will be used.

localCriterion: Criterion to filter local properties of the link. For a tabular attribute search, this will be a criterion against the local columns and so it will use column ids/guids instead of attribute ones. For other types of link, this is currently unused.

indirectLinks: For static and cross database links: whether the search should consider indirect links between records. The default is to decide based on the definition of the links

innerCriterion: Criterion to run to filter the linked records. When running linked search for tabular attribute we are searching against actual records and attributes, so attribute ids/guids should be used instead of column ids/guids.

localRowsBehavior: For tabular searching: Additional row filtering behavior for a search against local columns, or a tabular data exists search.

  • crossDatabaseLink: Links records across multiple databases.

  • ItemAdded: An item has been added to a list.

  • ListPublished: The status of the list was set to 'published'.
  • ListUnpublished: The status of the list was set to 'unpublished'.
  • ListRevisionCreated: A revision of a list was created.
  • UserSubscribed: A user subscribed to a list.
  • UserUnsubscribed: A user subscribed to a list.
  • ListCuratorAdded: Permissions changed - a user was set as curator for a list.
  • ListCuratorRemoved: Permissions changed - a user was removed as a curator for a list.
  • ListAdminAdded: Permissions changed - a user was set as admin for a list.
  • ListAdminRemoved: Permissions changed - a user was removed as an admin for a list.
  • ListPublisherAdded: Permissions changed - a user was set a publisher for a list.

the aggregation scope that have a value for the local column. In some cases, depending on the datum

also provide the minimum and maximum values that local column takes across records in the aggregation

including summary information about the values assumed by the local column.
            
For a numeric local column (integer, point, range, or date-time), the summary information will
be the minimum and maximum values assumed by the local column.
            
For a simple text local column (discrete, short-text), the summary information will be the most
common terms in the search index for that local column.

  • defaultExpressionNotFound: Default expression must be from attribute's expressions.
  • defaultFreeParameterNotFound: Default free parameter must be from attribute's parameters.
  • duplicateExpressionGuids: No duplicate expression GUIDs allowed.

  • expressionsHaveUnknownParameters: Parameter lists lacks some parameters required by the chosen expressions.
  • noExpressions: Maths functional attribute must have at least one expression or have 'allow anonymous expressions' set to true.

guid.description:
The GUID of this object. The GUID represents the object on a semantic level, and two objects of
the same type with the same GUID are considered to represent "the same concept". GUIDs should be
robust against data changes and database upgrades, and should be preferred where possible.

name.description:
The name of this object. The name represents the object at a human-readable level, but two objects of
the same type with the same need not represent "the same concept". Because the name is less uniquely identifying,
clients should prefer GUIDs where possible, and operations based on name instead of GUID may fail if the name
cannot be uniquely resolved. Certain object types may consider names to be equivalent

identity.description:
The underlying identity of this object. This represents the object at a data level, and two objects
of the same type with the same identity are considered to represent "the same object". However, identities
are not robust against database upgrades, and are only reliable and consistent within a currently-
loaded database in a running MI instance. Clients should prefer GUIDs where possible, and operations
based on identity which persist data will be resolved to GUIDs instead (and may fail if this cannot
be done).

GsaObjectIdentifier.description:
Properties that identify an object within the MI system.
            
An Granta.Server.Api.ObjectIdentifier created by MI will always contain values for all three
properties. An Granta.Server.Api.ObjectIdentifier created by a client need not contain values for
all three properties, and is allowed to contain values or combinations of values that do
not correspond to an existing object in MI (in which case the Granta.Server.Api.ObjectIdentifier
will be resolved against MI objects first by GUID, and then by name, and finally by identity,
taking the first match and ignoring subsequent fields.

keepAliveInMinutes.description: The length of time that the paginated search should be kept in memory

pageNumber.description: (Optional) the (1-indexed) number of the page to return from the search. No pages are returned if not provided

GsaPagingOptions.description: An optional field for paging options. If provided on a request, the response will contain an identifier that can be used to retrieve the other pages. Page size must be smaller than 10,000

Note: for legacy reasons, some 'record properties' do not fall into these criteria, and do
represent editable record fields more similar to attribute data. These record properties are

GsaUpdateRunStatus.description:
Represents the possible states of an update.

Possible values:

  • Registered: The update token has been registered with the service.
  • UploadInProgress: The update file has been partially uploaded.
  • Uploaded: The update file has been completely uploaded.
  • UploadFailed: The upload failed.
  • DryRunPending: A dry run for this update has been queued, but it not yet in progress.
  • DryRunCancelling: A request to cancel the dry run for this update has been issued but the dry run has not yet been cancelled.
  • DryRunCancelled: The dry run for this update was cancelled.
  • DryRunInProgress: The dry run for this update is in progress.
  • DryRunComplete: The dry run for this update is complete.
  • DryRunFailed: The dry run for this update failed.
  • ApplyPending: An apply operation for this update has been queued, but is not yet in progress.
  • ApplyInProgress: The update is being applied to the target database.
  • ApplyCancelling: A request to cancel the apply process has been issued but the apply process has not yet been cancelled.
  • ApplyCancelled: The update was cancelled during the apply process.
  • ApplyComplete: The update was successfully applied to the target database.
  • ApplyFailed: The update was not successfully applied to the target database.
